text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 26 in history
604 - Saint Augustine, first Archbishop of Canterbury, died. He founded the Christian church in southern England.
735 - The Venerable Bede, English monk and historian, died. His "Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum" is one of the main authorities on the history of England.
1521 - The Edict of Worms outlawed Martin Luther and his followers, following his Papal excommunication in April.
1650 - Duke of Marlborough, British military commander, born as John Churchill. One of England's greatest commanders he had significant victories over Louis XIV of France.
1659 - Aurangzeb formally ascended the Mogul throne.
1703 - Samuel Pepys, British diarist, died. His diary covered the years from 1659 to 1669.
1798 - During the Irish Rebellion the British killed about 500 Irish insurgents at the Battle of Tara.
1805 - Napoleon was crowned king of Italy in Milan cathedral.
1834 - The Portuguese Civil war ended with the capitulation of the pretender, Dom Miguel
1865 - The last Confederate resistance of the American Civil War ended when General Kirby Smith surrendered at New Orleans. The Confederates had already signed a surrender on April 9.
1867 - Princess Mary of Teck, queen consort of King George V of England, was born. Her children included the future kings Edward VIII and George VI.
1868 - Irish nationalist Michael Barrett was hanged for a bomb attack at Clerkenwell, London -- the last public execution in England.
1868 - U.S. President Andrew Johnson was finally acquitted of impeachment charges of "high crimes and misdemeanours".
1874 - Henri Farman, French aircraft designer who with his brother developed the biplane, born.
1879 - The British and Afghans signed the Treaty of Gandamak giving the British control of the Khyber Pass.
1886 - Al Jolson, entertainer and singer of such songs as "Mammy" and "Sonny Boy", was born in Russia as Asa Yoelson.
1907 - John Wayne, American actor known as "The Duke" famous for his portrayal of tough heroes in westerns, born as Marion Michael Morrison.
1912 - Janos Kadar, pro-Soviet Hungarian prime minister following the 1956 uprising, born
1923 - The first Le Mans 24-hour motor race was run.
1923 - James Arness, American actor best known for the TV series "Gunsmoke", born.
1940 - Operation Dynamo began to evacuate defeated Allied troops from Dunkirk.
1942 - Anglo-Soviet Treaty signed in London, providing for full collaboration during and after the Second World War.
1948 - The Nationalist Party took power in South African elections, beating the United Party by 70 seats to 65.
1966 - British Guiana became an independent member of the Commonwealth, changing its name to Guyana.
1971 - The Soviet Union's answer to Concorde, the TU-144, made its first appearance in the West at the Paris Air Show.
1979 - Finnish President Urho Kekkonen appointed a new coalition government with Mauno Koivisto as prime minister.
1982 - In the Falklands war, the British container ship Atlantic Conveyor and destroyer Coventry were both hit, killing 33.
1985 - Over 30 died when explosions destroyed two tankers off the coast of Gibraltar.
1991 - Zviad Gamsakhurdia was elected president of Georgia.
1991 - An Austrian Lauda-Air Boeing 767 crashed after a stopover in Bangkok, killing 223.
1993 - The Pakistan supreme court re-instated Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and parliament after they had been dissolved by President Ghulam Ishaq Khan.
1996 - Albania's opposition parties pulled out of the election on polling day because of "terror" and manipulation of the poll by the ruling Democratic Party.
